villager.name: Villager
villager.desc: Gathers food, wood and gold; builds structures. Defenseless in a real fight.

militia.name: Man-at-Arms
militia.desc: Cheap, sturdy frontline infantry. Closes on archers; melts to massed cavalry.

spearman.name: Spearman
spearman.desc: Anti-cavalry specialist. Brutal vs knights, weak against everything else.

archer.name: Archer
archer.desc: Ranged damage that shreds infantry. Fragile — keep it back, fear the cavalry.

skirmisher.name: Skirmisher
skirmisher.desc: Cheap anti-archer ranged unit. Counters bowmen; poor against everything melee.

horseman.name: Horseman
horseman.desc: Light melee cavalry. Fast and cheap — charges down archers and siege, and arrives a whole age before the Knight. Spears gut it. (Banner Age)

shieldbearer.name: Shieldbearer
shieldbearer.desc: A wall on legs. Hits softly, but soaks punishment that would fell anyone else. (Banner Age)

berserker.name: Berserker
berserker.desc: All edge and no guard — the hardest-hitting foot soldier alive, for as long as he stays alive. (Crown Age)

longbow.name: Longbowman
longbow.desc: Reaches further than anything else on two legs. Slow to draw, and helpless once caught. (Crown Age)

cataphract.name: Cataphract
cataphract.desc: Horse and rider both in scale. Rolls through a line and barely notices the spears. (Crown Age)

battlemage.name: Battlemage
battlemage.desc: Calls down fire that scatters a packed formation. Frail, slow to cast, and worth guarding. (Crown Age)

bombard.name: Bombard
bombard.desc: A siege gun on a carriage. Flattens buildings and anything unlucky enough to be near them. (Empire Age)

crossbow.name: Crossbowman
crossbow.desc: Heavy ranged punch. Outranges and outshoots the Archer; the backbone of a Crown-age line. (Crown Age)

knight.name: Knight
knight.desc: Fast, heavy cavalry. Runs down archers, siege and villagers. Hates spears.

catapult.name: Catapult
catapult.desc: Long-range siege. Devastates buildings and tight formations; helpless up close.

ram.name: Battering Ram
ram.desc: Armored siege engine built to break walls and buildings. Slow and clumsy vs troops.

trade_cart.name: Trade Cart
trade_cart.desc: Runs gold between two of your Markets, or an ally's. Pays by distance — a long, well-guarded route is a second economy. Unarmed.

hero.name: Champion
hero.desc: Your unique hero. Towering in a fight, grows stronger with every kill, and rises again at your Town Center if he falls.

trebuchet.name: Trebuchet
trebuchet.desc: Siege artillery with colossal range. Levels walls and towers from beyond their reach — but glacially slow and helpless up close. (Empire Age)

monk.name: Monk
monk.desc: Crown-age support. Heals nearby allies over time. No frontline value.

javelin.name: Javelin Thrower
javelin.desc: Hurls heavy javelins — hits harder than an archer but at shorter range. Punishes cavalry that close on it. (Banner Age)

handcannon.name: Hand Cannoneer
handcannon.desc: Gunpowder marksman. Enormous range and a punishing shot, but reloads slowly — devastating massed, helpless if rushed. (Empire Age)

raider.name: Raider
raider.desc: Light, lightning-fast cavalry built to butcher villagers and wreck an economy. Fragile in a real fight — strike and run. (Banner Age)

scout.name: Scout
scout.desc: A swift outrider with keen eyes. Cheap early scouting and light harassment — no match for real soldiers.

twohand.name: Two-Handed Swordsman
twohand.desc: Elite heavy infantry with a greatsword — the top of the foot-soldier line. Cleaves infantry and buildings; still wary of massed cavalry. (Crown Age)

king.name: King
king.desc: Your sovereign. In Regicide, protect your King and slay the enemy's to win. Sturdy and brave, but losing him loses the game.

pikeman.name: Pikeman
pikeman.desc: A disciplined pike block — even deadlier to cavalry than the spearman, and it keeps spears relevant against Crown-age knights. (Crown Age)

sworn_blade.name: Sworn Blade
sworn_blade.desc: Oath of the Sword. Quick, hard-hitting swordsmen who arrive an age before the Two-Handed — built to strike an enemy before it is ready. (Banner Age)

lancer.name: Lancer
lancer.desc: Oath of the Lance. Heavy horse with a couched lance: the first blow after a run hits three times as hard. Let it ride in; don't let it stand and trade. (Crown Age)

ranger.name: Ranger
ranger.desc: Oath of the Bow. A woodland archer who stays hidden among the trees even while shooting — an ambush that doesn't give itself away. (Crown Age)

halberdier.name: Halberdier
halberdier.desc: Oath of the Shield. Pike and axe on one haft: murderous to cavalry, and it chops rams apart. Slow, and no match for swords. (Crown Age)

great_bombard.name: Great Bombard
great_bombard.desc: Oath of the Engine. A cannon too big for a carriage, dragged into place and fired from beyond any tower's reach. Painfully slow; guard it. (Empire Age)

royal_guard.name: Royal Guard
royal_guard.desc: Oath of the Crown. Plate-clad household troops — the toughest foot soldiers in the realm, and good against almost anything that isn't massed siege. (Empire Age)

yeoman.name: Longbowman
yeoman.desc: The Kingdom. Outranges every archer in the field; slow to draw and no good up close. (Crown Age)

legionary.name: Legionary
legionary.desc: The Legion. Takes the Man-at-Arms' place: a tall shield that turns arrows, and the discipline to hold. A touch slower.

samurai.name: Samurai
samurai.desc: The Shogunate. Takes the Two-Handed Swordsman's place: better armoured and quicker with the blade, and priced like it. (Crown Age)

horse_archer.name: Horse Archer
horse_archer.desc: The Khanate. Shoots from the saddle and never stops moving — hard to catch, fragile if you do. (Banner Age)

pulse_trooper.name: Pulse Trooper
pulse_trooper.desc: The Ascendancy. Takes the Crossbowman's place: an energy rifle with a flat, punishing shot. Costly, as everything of theirs is. (Crown Age)

skimmer.name: Skimmer
skimmer.desc: The Ascendancy. Takes the Horseman's place: a hover-sled rider, the fastest thing on the field — a raider and a siege-hunter. (Banner Age)

town_center.desc: Heart of your realm. Trains villagers, drops off all resources, garrisons your people.
town_center.name: Town Center

house.desc: Raises your population limit by 10 so you can field a larger force.
house.name: House

mill.desc: Food drop-off. Build it next to berries, farms or hunt to save villager walking time.
mill.name: Mill

lumber_camp.desc: Wood drop-off. Plant it in the trees to keep your woodline efficient.
lumber_camp.name: Lumber Camp

mining_camp.desc: Gold drop-off. Build beside a gold vein to mine efficiently.
mining_camp.name: Mining Camp

farm.desc: A renewable source of food. Villagers work the field around it.
farm.name: Farm

bridge.desc: A timber crossing over shallows. Troops cross at full speed instead of wading. Cannot be built on dry land.
bridge.name: Bridge

barracks.desc: Trains infantry — Men-at-Arms and anti-cavalry Spearmen.
barracks.name: Barracks

archery_range.desc: Trains ranged units — Archers and anti-archer Skirmishers. (Banner Age)
archery_range.name: Archery Range

blacksmith.desc: Improves your military with attack and armor upgrades. (Banner Age)
blacksmith.name: Blacksmith

market.desc: Trade resources for gold, and home for Trade Carts. Prices move with what everyone is selling. (Banner Age)
market.name: Market

stable.desc: Trains Horsemen now, and Knights once you reach the Crown Age. (Banner Age)
stable.name: Stable

siege_workshop.desc: Builds Catapults and Battering Rams to crack fortifications. (Crown Age)
siege_workshop.name: Siege Workshop

watch_tower.desc: Ranged defensive tower. Garrison units to add arrows. (Banner Age)
watch_tower.name: Watch Tower

watchfire.desc: A beacon that burns through the dark. Wide sight the night can't dim — light up your walls and the approaches to your base.
watchfire.name: Watchfire

palisade.desc: Cheap wooden wall. Throws up fast to seal a gap or screen your villagers.
palisade.name: Palisade

stone_wall.desc: Tough stone rampart. The backbone of a fortress. (Banner Age)
stone_wall.name: Stone Wall

gate.desc: Opens for your troops, shuts against the enemy. Sally out, then bar the door. (Banner Age)
gate.name: Gate

castle.desc: Towering fortress. Heavy arrow fire, huge garrison, trains Monks. (Crown Age)
castle.name: Castle

iron_casting.name: Iron Casting
iron_casting.desc: +2 attack for infantry and cavalry. (Crown Age)

chain_mail.name: Chain Mail Armor
chain_mail.desc: +1 armor for infantry and cavalry. (Crown Age)

bodkin_arrow.name: Bodkin Arrow
bodkin_arrow.desc: +2 attack for archers and towers. (Crown Age)

pikes.name: Pikes
pikes.desc: Spearmen & Pikemen +12 bonus damage vs cavalry. (Crown Age)

horse_collar.name: Horse Collar
horse_collar.desc: Farms & foraging yield 18% more food. (Banner Age)

loom.name: Loom
loom.desc: Villagers gain +15 HP — raids stop being free. (Hearth Age)

town_watch.name: Town Watch
town_watch.desc: Everything you own sees 25% further. (Banner Age)

treadmill_crane.name: Treadmill Crane
treadmill_crane.desc: Villagers build and repair 20% faster. (Crown Age)

caravan.name: Caravan
caravan.desc: Market trades return 85 instead of 75. (Crown Age)

blast_furnace.name: Blast Furnace
blast_furnace.desc: +2 attack for infantry and cavalry. (Empire Age)

plate_mail.name: Plate Mail Armor
plate_mail.desc: +2 armor for infantry and cavalry. (Empire Age)

bracer.name: Bracer
bracer.desc: +2 attack for archers and towers. (Empire Age)

crop_rotation.name: Crop Rotation
crop_rotation.desc: Farms & foraging yield 15% more food. (Empire Age)

kingdom.name: The Kingdom
kingdom.tagline: Castles, knights and the longbow — slow to start, hard to stop.
strengths: Castles and Watch Towers cost 20% less
Longbowmen at the Archery Range (Crown Age)

guide.playstyle: The most forgiving realm to learn on. Nothing about the Kingdom is flashy in the first ten minutes — it builds, walls up and researches — but cheap Blacksmith upgrades mean every soldier it fields in the Crown and Empire ages hits harder and lasts longer than anyone else's, and cheap castles let it hold ground it takes. Longbowmen shoot farther than any crossbow or Pulse Trooper.
suits: You want to learn the game without being punished for it
You like walls, castles and a strong late army
You prefer winning big fights over raiding
tips: Get to the Crown Age — your bonuses are worth most there
Spend the Blacksmith discount: every upgrade, every age
A castle at a choke point is cheap for you and very expensive for them
Longbowmen behind knights or spearmen win most open fights
guide.struggles: Early aggression — the Jarls and the Khanate hit before your bonuses matter. Wall and hold the first ten minutes.

legion.name: The Legion
legion.tagline: Engineers and heavy infantry — the shield wall that builds a road behind it.
strengths: Legionaries replace the Man-at-Arms — they shrug off arrows

guide.playstyle: An engineer's army. The Legion builds faster than anyone, so its economy and its forward bases come online early, and its Legionaries replace the Man-at-Arms with a heavier soldier that shrugs off arrows. It is at its best in the middle of the match, pushing a wall of shields forward and building towers and barracks right behind it.
suits: You like a solid infantry line that just walks forward
You like building forward — towers, barracks, walls near the enemy
You want a strong mid-game rather than an all-in rush
tips: Legionaries beat archer-heavy armies: take fights into their arrows
Build a forward barracks — you put it up faster than they can react
Shieldbearers screen your line while it advances
Avoid mass cavalry: it costs you 15% more
guide.struggles: Fast cavalry that refuses to fight your line and raids behind it, and very late armies with full upgrades.

norse.name: The Jarls
norse.tagline: Fast feet and axes — burn them out before they are ready.
strengths: Infantry deal 25% more damage to buildings
Berserkers at the Barracks from the Banner Age

guide.playstyle: Raiders. The Jarls' infantry run faster and tear buildings down a quarter faster than anyone else's, their woodcutters are quicker, and Berserkers arrive as soon as the Banner Age. The whole faction is built to hit early and keep hitting — burn houses, kill villagers, make the enemy fight on your schedule. Let the game run long and your smithing and castles cost more than theirs.
suits: You like to attack first and never stop
You enjoy raiding, burning and hit-and-run
You would rather end the game early than out-tech anyone
tips: Take Berserkers the moment the Banner Age lands and go
Target houses and the Town Centre's farms — your infantry burns them fast
Keep raiding in two places at once; fast feet make that possible
If the enemy walls up, switch to rams rather than waiting
guide.struggles: Walls and towers, and any opponent who survives to the Crown Age with an economy intact.

shogunate.name: The Shogunate
shogunate.tagline: Fewer soldiers, better ones — every blade is a master's.

guide.playstyle: Fewer soldiers, better ones. Every Shogunate soldier has more HP and every melee soldier strikes faster, the villagers are a quarter tougher, and Samurai replace the Two-Handed Swordsman as the finest duellists in the game. The price is time: soldiers train slower, so every loss hurts and the army has to be used well rather than thrown away.
suits: You like controlling small, elite armies carefully
You win by good engagements rather than bigger numbers
You want villagers that survive early raids
tips: Never trade evenly — pick fights where your quality decides it
Pull units back when they are hurt; replacing them is slow
Samurai win most infantry duels: send them at the enemy's foot soldiers
Your villagers survive raids that would kill others' — keep them working longer
guide.struggles: Being out-numbered by cheap mass armies, and long wars of attrition where train time decides it.

khanate.name: The Khanate
khanate.tagline: The whole realm rides — strike anywhere, never stand still.
strengths: Stables and Archery Ranges cost 25% less
Horse Archers from the Banner Age; Cataphracts at the Stable

guide.playstyle: The whole realm rides. Khanate cavalry are the fastest in the game, Stables and Archery Ranges are cheap, and Horse Archers arrive as early as the Banner Age with Cataphracts later. It wins by movement — raiding where the enemy isn't, and refusing fights it doesn't want. Its buildings are flimsy and walls expensive, so it has to attack rather than hold.
suits: You like fast units and hit-and-run
You are happy to micro-manage a moving army
You would rather be everywhere than defend one place
tips: Horse Archers kite infantry forever — never let them catch you
Raid villagers, not buildings
Yurts house 13: fewer houses means more for the army
Don't turtle — your buildings are 20% weaker; defend by counter-attacking
guide.struggles: Spearmen, pikemen and walls, and anyone who forces a stand-up fight at a choke point.

ascendancy.name: The Ascendancy
ascendancy.tagline: Stranded star-farers with better tools and fewer hands.
strengths: Pulse Troopers replace the Crossbowman; Skimmers replace the Horseman

guide.playstyle: Stranded star-farers with better tools and fewer hands. Villagers carry 40% more, so the economy grows with fewer workers, and buildings repair themselves when left alone. Pulse Troopers replace the Crossbowman and Skimmers replace the Horseman — both better than what they stand in for. Everything military costs 15% more, so the Ascendancy plays a patient, efficient game and wins late.
suits: You like a strong economy and a patient build-up
You want high-tech units that out-class what they face
You like the game going long
tips: Fewer villagers carrying more — spend the saving on getting to the next age
Once a raid is beaten off, leave the damage — your buildings mend themselves
Pulse Troopers out-class the Crossbowmen they replace — make them your ranged core
Skimmers are your scouts and raiders early
guide.struggles: Early rushes — soldiers cost more and there are fewer of them at the start.

signature.title: Endless Fields
signature.text: Farms replant themselves at no cost

coin.name: Oath of the Coin
coin.motto: Every road leads to our markets.

signature.title: The Tithe
signature.text: Your Markets pay gold whether or not anyone trades

steward.name: Aldric
steward.title: The Steward
steward.desc: A master of the early game. Begins each match with two extra villagers already at work.

quartermaster.name: Mirelle
quartermaster.title: The Quartermaster
quartermaster.desc: Nothing is wasted under her ledger. Every villager gathers 15% faster, all game.

architect.name: Doryan
architect.title: The Architect
architect.desc: Raises walls and halls in a blink — your villagers build and repair twice as fast.

marshal.name: Sir Garron
marshal.title: The Marshal
marshal.desc: Drills a hardier host. Every soldier you field has +8% health and +1 armor.

magnate.name: Cassia
magnate.title: The Magnate
magnate.desc: Old coin opens every door. Start with a tidy stockpile of food, wood and gold.

drillmaster.name: Vasco
drillmaster.title: The Drillmaster
drillmaster.desc: Forges veterans from recruits — your units earn veterancy 40% faster from kills.

warden.name: Brenna
warden.title: The Warden
warden.desc: Plans for a siege from the first dawn. Begin with +10 population headroom and +1 unit armor.

banneret.name: Lady Yorath
banneret.title: The Banneret
banneret.desc: Plants a rallying standard: villagers near it gather 15% faster and soldiers are bolstered and mended.

power.name: Rally Banner
power.desc: Plant a banner: friendly villagers nearby gather +15% and soldiers gain +2 armor and steady healing for 20s.

warpriest.name: Father Edmun
warpriest.title: The Warpriest
warpriest.desc: Raises a holy standard that knits wounds fast — strong battlefield healing where it stands.

power.name: Holy Standard
power.desc: Plant a sacred standard: nearby soldiers gain +1 armor and heal rapidly for 18s.

hero.name: Heroic Cleave
hero.desc: A sweeping blow: heavy damage to all enemies around the Champion, and a rallying surge for nearby allies.

villager.name: Take Cover
villager.desc: Down tools and run! +8 armour and +50% speed for 5s to escape a raid and reach safety.

militia.name: War Cry
militia.desc: Bellow a rallying cry — every nearby ally hits 40% harder for 6s. Time it as the lines meet.

spearman.name: Brace Spears
spearman.desc: Set spears against a charge: +4 armour and devastating bonus damage to cavalry for 7s.

archer.name: Arrow Volley
archer.desc: Loose a massed volley that rains down on your target, striking everything around it at once.

skirmisher.name: Caltrops
skirmisher.desc: Scatter caltrops — every enemy nearby is slowed to a crawl for 4s. Kite them to death.

knight.name: Cavalry Charge
knight.desc: Spur the horses: +65% speed and +50% damage for 5s. Crash into archers and run down stragglers.

catapult.name: Burning Pitch
catapult.desc: Load incendiary shot: heavier rocks, hurled faster, for 8s. Flatten a base in a hurry.

ram.name: Battering Frenzy
ram.desc: The crew heaves in a fury — double the battering speed against walls and buildings for 6s.

twohand.name: Wide Arc
twohand.desc: A two-handed sweep that carves through every enemy pressed around him.

shieldbearer.name: Shield Wall
shieldbearer.desc: Shields up along the line: every nearby ally gains armour for 8s. He is why the line holds.

berserker.name: Blood Frenzy
berserker.desc: Works himself into a fury: strikes 60% faster and 30% harder for 6s. No guard at all.

pikeman.name: Pike Hedge
pikeman.desc: Level the pikes — everything nearby is bogged down for 5s, and cavalry is gutted on the points.

crossbow.name: Pavise
crossbow.desc: Plant the shield and wind the windlass: +6 armour and 40% faster bolts for 7s, rooted in place.

longbow.name: Arrow Storm
longbow.desc: The sky goes dark: a wide, punishing fall of arrows across the enemy formation.

handcannon.name: Scattershot
handcannon.desc: Cram the barrel with scrap and fire: a brutal cone of shot that shreds packed infantry.

javelin.name: Volley of Spears
javelin.desc: Loose the whole bundle at once — heavy damage, and cavalry take the worst of it.

horseman.name: Run Them Down
horseman.desc: Spur into the shooters: +55% speed and savage bonus damage to archers for 5s.

raider.name: Put to the Torch
raider.desc: Burn as you pass: +50% speed and heavy bonus damage to villagers and buildings for 6s.

scout.name: Outrider
scout.desc: Break into a gallop: +80% speed and +4 armour for 5s. For getting out, not getting stuck in.

cataphract.name: Iron Wedge
cataphract.desc: Lower the lances and drive through: +8 armour and +45% damage for 6s.

battlemage.name: Firestorm
battlemage.desc: Calls fire down across a wide stretch of the field. Devastating on a packed formation.

bombard.name: Point Blank
bombard.desc: Depress the barrel and touch it off: an enormous blast that levels whatever is in front of it.

trebuchet.name: Full Counterweight
trebuchet.desc: Wind it to the stops: far heavier stones, thrown faster, for 9s.

monk.name: Sanctuary
monk.desc: A pulse of holy light instantly heals every ally around the monk for 45 HP.

vanguard.name: Vanguard
vanguard.desc: Plants on the centre line and holds it. Your wall — nothing gets past without going through.

line.name: Line
line.desc: Marches straight across and pushes into the enemy formation.

flanker.name: Flanker
flanker.desc: Sweeps along the edge of the field and comes in from the side, past the enemy front.

artillery.name: Artillery
artillery.desc: Never advances. Stands where you put it and shoots — so where you put it is the whole decision.

infiltrator.name: Infiltrator
infiltrator.desc: Opens the fight behind the enemy line, straight onto their archers and engines.

squire.name: Squire
squire.desc: A gentle introduction. Slow to act, never scouts, fields simple armies.

knight.name: Knight
knight.desc: A real opponent. Follows a solid build, defends itself, attacks on a timer.

lord.name: Lord
lord.desc: Scouts you, counters your army, expands, and pressures from two sides.

warlord.name: Warlord
warlord.desc: Relentless. Everything the Lord does, faster, with a stronger economy.

conqueror.name: Conqueror
conqueror.desc: The ultimate test. A booming economy, flawless micro, and waves that never stop.

BIOMES.name: Temperate
BIOMES.desc: Green country: grass, mixed woods, the odd lake.

BIOMES.name: Arid
BIOMES.desc: Dust and rock. Sparse woods, mountains everywhere.

BIOMES.name: Alpine
BIOMES.desc: Snow and stone, cut by high ridges and cold lakes.

BIOMES.name: Wetland
BIOMES.desc: Low, wet ground — marsh, shallows and thick forest.

TERRAIN_DEFS.name: Dirt
TERRAIN_DEFS.desc: Bare earth — a road or a worn patch.

TERRAIN_DEFS.name: Lake
TERRAIN_DEFS.desc: Deep water. Impassable — armies go around.

TERRAIN_DEFS.name: Forest
TERRAIN_DEFS.desc: Passable but slow, and you can't see far in. Nothing builds here.

TERRAIN_DEFS.name: Mountain
TERRAIN_DEFS.desc: Sheer rock. Impassable — the hardest barrier there is.

TERRAIN_DEFS.name: Hill
TERRAIN_DEFS.desc: High ground: slower to climb, but sees and shoots 20% further.

TERRAIN_DEFS.name: Marsh
TERRAIN_DEFS.desc: Boggy. Slow going and nothing to show for it.

TERRAIN_DEFS.name: Shallows
TERRAIN_DEFS.desc: Fordable water. Crossable, and a terrible place to be caught.

PRESETS.name: Open Plains
PRESETS.desc: Wide open grassland. Armies clash early and often — cavalry country.

PRESETS.name: Black Forest
PRESETS.desc: Dense woods carve natural walls. Turtle up, then break through.

PRESETS.name: Riverlands
PRESETS.desc: A winding river splits the field. Control the crossings.

PRESETS.name: Highlands
PRESETS.desc: Rolling country dotted with ponds and copses. A balanced all-rounder.

PRESETS.name: Islands
PRESETS.desc: Lakes carve the land into linked holds. Fight over the land bridges.

PRESETS.name: Crossroads
PRESETS.desc: A small, near-bare arena. No room to hide — the better army wins, fast.

PRESETS.name: Gauntlet
PRESETS.desc: Forest barriers funnel every attack through narrow lanes. Hold the gap.

SYMMETRIES.label: Rotate 180°
SYMMETRIES.desc: The classic two-player mirror: both halves are identical ground.

SYMMETRIES.label: Quarters
SYMMETRIES.desc: Four-way — for a four-player map with equal corners.

SYMMETRIES.label: Radial ×3
SYMMETRIES.desc: Three equal slices around the centre. Stay inside the circle that fits the map — corners rotate off the edge.

SYMMETRIES.label: Radial ×6
SYMMETRIES.desc: Six equal slices. Stay inside the circle that fits the map — corners rotate off the edge.

SYMMETRIES.label: Radial ×8
SYMMETRIES.desc: Eight equal slices, one per seat on a full lobby. Corners rotate off the edge.

MAP_SIZES.label: Duel
MAP_SIZES.desc: A closed arena. Bases within sight of each other — first fight decides it.

MAP_SIZES.label: Skirmish
MAP_SIZES.desc: Very small. Room for a wall and a woodline, not much more.

MAP_SIZES.label: Tiny
MAP_SIZES.desc: Cramped. Expansions are contested from the first minute.

MAP_SIZES.label: Small
MAP_SIZES.desc: Tight but complete — the classic aggressive 1v1 size.

MAP_SIZES.label: Medium
MAP_SIZES.desc: The standard field. Comfortable for two to four.

MAP_SIZES.label: Large
MAP_SIZES.desc: Room to manoeuvre, and a real map to scout.

MAP_SIZES.label: Huge
MAP_SIZES.desc: Long games. Expansions matter more than the opening.

MAP_SIZES.label: Massive
MAP_SIZES.desc: A campaign map. Armies take a while to arrive anywhere.

MAP_SIZES.label: Colossal
MAP_SIZES.desc: Enormous. A corner-to-corner march is most of a minute at full speed.

NOMAD_RULES.label: Never
NOMAD_RULES.desc: This map is played from its authored spawn points.

NOMAD_RULES.label: Allowed
NOMAD_RULES.desc: Spawn points are used normally; a nomad game ignores them and drops everyone at random.

NOMAD_RULES.label: Always nomad
NOMAD_RULES.desc: There are no spawn points. Everyone lands somewhere random, every game.

maps/script.EXAMPLE_SCRIPT:
# Highland Passes — a family of maps, not one map.
size 128
biome alpine
seats 4
symmetry quad

base grass
blob meadow count 40 radius 2-5
blob mountain count 10 radius 4-8
blob hill count 22 radius 3-6
blob forest count 26 radius 3-6
lake water count 4 radius 4-8
river shallow width 3

# Seats first: the clusters below are placed relative to them.
spawns ring radius 0.34

cluster berries count 1 near start radius 6-10 nodes 6
cluster gold count 2 near start radius 20-40 nodes 5
cluster tree count 4 near start radius 10-18 nodes 8
scatter tree count 260

SCRIPT_COMMANDS.name: size
SCRIPT_COMMANDS.desc: Map width in cells, 40–320. Rounded to the nearest size preset is not required — any number works.

SCRIPT_COMMANDS.name: biome
SCRIPT_COMMANDS.desc: Which palette the map is painted from.

SCRIPT_COMMANDS.name: seats
SCRIPT_COMMANDS.desc: How many players the map is for, 1–8.

SCRIPT_COMMANDS.name: symmetry
SCRIPT_COMMANDS.desc: Every placement is repeated through this. rot180 is the classic 1v1 mirror.

SCRIPT_COMMANDS.name: base
SCRIPT_COMMANDS.desc: Fill the whole map with one ground before anything else.

SCRIPT_COMMANDS.name: blob
SCRIPT_COMMANDS.desc: Organic patches — the workhorse. Also spelled patch, lake or range; all the same.

SCRIPT_COMMANDS.name: ring
SCRIPT_COMMANDS.desc: A band at a fraction of the way out from the centre. Moats, crater rims, a central plateau edge.

SCRIPT_COMMANDS.name: river
SCRIPT_COMMANDS.desc: A wandering line from one edge to the other.

SCRIPT_COMMANDS.name: spawns
SCRIPT_COMMANDS.desc: Seat every player evenly around a circle.

SCRIPT_COMMANDS.name: spawn
SCRIPT_COMMANDS.desc: Seat one player at an exact cell (repeated through symmetry).

SCRIPT_COMMANDS.name: cluster
SCRIPT_COMMANDS.desc: n clusters of k nodes per seat, at a distance between a and b cells.

SCRIPT_COMMANDS.name: scatter
SCRIPT_COMMANDS.desc: Nodes strewn across the whole map.
